status.en: 10 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 57% fewer than the week before, most of them in Niamey, Kidal and Anefis.
status.nb: 10 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 57 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Niamey, Kidal og Anefis.

summary.en: Islamist militants in Nigeria killed 24 Christians in an overnight attack and expanded Lakurawa bases into South Kebbi, while Fulanis killed and kidnapped Christians in Kaduna State. Russian forces retook Kidal and Mali announced a recapture of the city without fighting, indicating renewed external military involvement. Niger expelled French intelligence agents, increasing diplomatic tension in the region. The conflict produced 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Islamske militante i Nigeria drepte 24 kristne i et overnattingsangrep og utvidet Lakurawa-baser til Sør‑Kebbi, mens fulani drepte og kidnappet kristne i Kaduna‑delstaten. Russiske styrker tok Kidal tilbake og Mali kunngjorde at byen var gjenerobret uten kamp, noe som indikerer fornyet utenlandsk militær involvering. Niger utviste franske etterretningsagenter, noe som øker den diplomatiske spenningen i regionen. Konflikten førte til 4 159 dødsfall i kamprelaterte handlinger i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.extract: The War in the Sahel, also known synonymously as the Sahel War is a multi-sided armed conflict that has been ongoing since 2012. In particular, the intensive conflict mainly takes place in the three countries of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso.
